overclaims: Earlier reviews found limited evidence, while a 16-week trial reported some benefits.
checks.note: Excerpt, proposition, criteria, axis/outcome/horizon (historical_observation, not_applicable, unresolved) and the e1/e2 citations all match. But the rationale says 'Earlier reviews' (plural), and the evidence has only one review: the 2020 JMIR systematic review (e1). The 403'd Wiley review was never read. This overstates the evidence base. The limitation calling the two blocked sources 'several relevant full-text sources' is also loose: they were separate sources, not full texts of the abstracts that were read.

The excerpt is the speaker's exact clause, and the social media comparison is shown in the proposition and from_speaker. Axis forecast_outcome, open_horizon, unresolved match the reviews. Rationale claims map to e2 (no social media comparison), e3 (Reddit-based, no consensus definition) and e4 (problematic use correlates with symptoms). Citation fragments, dates and relations match the frozen items. 'Empirically grounded' is close to the line but stays near e4's 'consistent with' framing.
